ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The upper circuit in the figure is labeled as input resistance R_A, and is a ladder network extending infinitely to the right: the upper branch has 2Ω series resistors in sequence, and each node is connected downward through a 1Ω resistor to the bottom common rail. The lower circuit is labeled as input resistance R_B and also extends infinitely to the right; its input-end top node, in addition to being connected to the same 2Ω series ladder network to the right, is also directly connected through a 1Ω resistor to the bottom rail. Reasoning: Looking into the input end of the lower circuit, there are two parallel branches: one is this 1Ω resistor at the left end directly connected to ground; the other is the network entered to the right from the input end. The structure of this rightward network is the same as the R_A network defined above, so its equivalent input resistance is R_A. Therefore R_B = 1Ω || R_A. By the parallel formula, R_B = (1·R_A)/(1 + R_A) = R_A/(1 + R_A), where the resistance is in ohms.
